hook: VA Awards Tria Federal *$120M* Task Order
dek: Four-year deal expands support for veteran community care across the VHA.

slides.label: What happened
slides.text: The VA awarded Tria Federal a four-year, *$120 million* task order for VHA community care support.

slides.label: Who's involved
slides.text: Tria Federal, based in *Arlington, Virginia*, has supported VA community care for over a decade.

slides.label: What they'll do
slides.text: Tria will handle *contract oversight*, utilization management, clinical guidance and network monitoring.

slides.label: The bigger program
slides.text: Work falls under the VHA Veteran Community Care Program Support *BPA*, covering new healthcare contracts.

slides.label: By the numbers
slides.text: Community care now costs *$50 billion* a year, up from less than $2 billion a decade ago.

slides.label: Growing fast
slides.text: Community-based care is *45%* of veteran healthcare visits and expected to pass 50% soon.

slides.label: Leadership voice
slides.text: CEO Tim Borchert said the goal is getting veterans *the right care* at the right cost.

slides.label: Why it matters
slides.text: Deals like this show how trust in government work can grow into *major contracts*, something underrepresented founders eyeing federal work should watch.

caption_instagram:
$120 million. One task order. One company built on trust with the VA.

Tria Federal, headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, just landed a four-year deal to keep running community care support for the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). The work includes contract oversight, utilization management and building out new payment models for veteran care.

This isn't new territory for them. Tria has backed VA community care for over a decade, watching it grow from under $2 billion a year to more than $50 billion today. CEO Tim Borchert says the mission stays the same: getting veterans the right care, through the right provider, at the right cost.

Federal contracts like this prove that long-term relationships and consistent delivery can turn into serious revenue, a lesson worth studying for any founder chasing government work.

The VA just handed Tria Federal a four-year, $120 million task order to continue supporting community care operations at the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), per GovConWire.

The scope: contract oversight, utilization management, clinical guidance, network performance monitoring and development of an alternative payment model for veteran care.

Context matters here. Tria has supported VA community care for more than a decade, a period in which the program grew from under $2 billion a year to over $50 billion. Community-based care now makes up more than 45 percent of veteran healthcare encounters and is projected to top 50 percent soon.

CEO Tim Borchert framed the award as proof of long-term trust built with the agency.

For founders and operators building in the federal space, this is a case study in what sustained performance can turn into: bigger scope, bigger contracts, bigger trust.
